about: What a fips exit's advert on Nostr says, and what a byte costs: the cases every implementation is held to. What each case expects was written out case by case, not produced by one of the implementations; the file is read by payd/proto (Rust), by fips-exit advert (Python) and by the clients. Everything outside ASCII is written as an escape, since some of it cannot be seen. 'write' is an advert, the time it is written at, and the tags an exit writes for it, in that order, or no tags when it must refuse to. 'read' is an event's tags, its date and the reader's clock, and the advert a client makes of them, or null when it must pass the event over. 'tidy' is a name or a note as an advert carries it, the most characters it may have, and what a reader shows; an exit may write only text that is already what a reader would show. 'price' is bytes, a price in millisatoshi per gigabyte of 10^9 bytes, and the millisatoshi due, rounded up.
